correctness.rationale: Braunfeld's age description makes a labelled injective \(n\)-substructure exactly a choice of an equivalence partition with \(k\) classes, a global order on all \(n\) points, and an independent order on the \(k\) classes; the within-class part of the second convex order is then forced. This gives \(n!\sum_k k!{n\brace k}=n!F_n\). For arbitrary tuples, the equality pattern contributes another Stirling transform. Using the classical asymptotic \(F_n\sim n!/[2(\log2)^{n+1}]\), fixed-defect partitions \({n\brace n-j}\sim n^{2j}/(2^j j!)\) contribute \(((\log2)/2)^j/j!\), while the remaining tail is negligible, so \(b_n/a_n\to e^{(\log2)/2}=\sqrt2\). The inspected verifier exactly enumerates the induced relation signatures through arity five and corroborates the asymptotic recurrence.

originality.rationale: Braunfeld already gives the complete finite-age description of the homogeneous structure. Homogeneity makes injective ordered-tuple orbits exactly the labelled finite structures in that age, and counting those objects is the direct product of a set partition, a point order, and a class order—the classical Fubini enumeration. The all-tuple Stirling transform is the standard equality-pattern passage, and the constant \(1/\sqrt2\) follows routinely from the classical ordered-Bell asymptotic. final_claim: For Braunfeld's exceptional homogeneous permutation structure of Example 2.7, the injective ordered \(n\)-tuple orbit count is \(a_n=n!F_n\), the all-tuple orbit count is its Stirling transform \(b_n=\sum_k {n\brace k}a_k\), and \(a_n/b_n\to1/\sqrt2\).
